title: PESA Class Aides & Child. Wartime Vets Funds
lastAction: Ref to the Com on Appropriations, if favorable, Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill makes two changes: (1) it allows Personal Education Student Account (PESA) scholarship funds to be used to pay for one-to-one classroom aides at private schools, with restrictions on who can serve as an aide, and (2) it appropriates $1 million for fiscal year 2025-2026 and $7 million for fiscal year 2026-2027 to increase and expand scholarships for children of wartime veterans.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue that allowing PESA funds for classroom aides helps students with specialized learning needs access personalized educational support in private school settings. They also contend that increasing wartime veterans' scholarships honors military service and provides educational opportunities for eligible veterans' children by restoring scholarship amounts that were previously reduced.
aiConArguments: Opponents may be concerned about accountability and oversight of one-to-one aides who are not school employees, questioning how their qualifications and performance are monitored. Others might argue that the $8 million in appropriated funds for veterans' scholarships, particularly the $7 million recurring commitment, could strain the state budget or be redirected to other educational priorities or needs.
